title: train(s) bus(es) (singular and plural)
subtitle: one flower / some flowers
summary: Make plurals with -s, learn the spelling rules for -es, -ies and -ves, and remember the special plurals like men, children and people.

lesson.heading: The plural is usually -s
lesson.text: *Singular* means one. *Plural* means two or more. One flower stands in a vase; in the next vase there are four flowers. For most nouns we just add **-s**.

lesson.heading: Spelling
rows: bus -> buses, dish -> dishes, church -> churches, box -> boxes
baby -> babies, dictionary -> dictionaries, party -> parties
day -> days, monkey -> monkeys, boy -> boys
shelf -> shelves, knife -> knives, wife -> wives

lesson.heading: Words that are always plural
lesson.text: These things are plural in English: **scissors**, **glasses**, **trousers**, **jeans**, **shorts**, **tights**, **pyjamas**. You can also say **a pair of** scissors / trousers / pyjamas.

examples.text: I need **a new pair of jeans**. *or* I need **some new jeans**.

lesson.heading: Some plurals do not end in -s
lesson.note: *She's a nice person*, but *They are nice people*, not ~~nice persons~~.

lesson.heading: people and police are plural
lesson.text: **people** means *they*, so we say **people are** and **people have**. **police** is plural too.

examples.text: I like the people here. **They are** very friendly.
The police **want** to talk to anybody who saw the accident.

lesson.text: *Many people are here*, not ~~is here~~. Think of *people* as *they*.

exercises.explanation: Words ending in -f or -fe change to -ves.

exercises.prompt: Match each singular word with its plural.
How do you spell the plural of these words?
Gary is standing at the mirror with a toothbrush. Gary is cleaning his ___.
exercises.explanation: The plural of tooth is teeth.

exercises.prompt: A man and two women are waiting at the bus stop. There are three ___ at the bus stop.
exercises.explanation: The plural of person is people.

exercises.statement: There was a woman in the car with two mens.
exercises.explanation: There was a woman in the car with two men. The plural of man is men, with no -s.

exercises.statement: We went fishing, but we didn't catch many fish.
exercises.explanation: fish is the same in the singular and the plural.

exercises.statement: I like your trouser. Where did you get it?
exercises.explanation: I like your trousers. Where did you get them? trousers is always plural.

exercises.prompt: A lot of people ___ television every day.
exercises.explanation: people is plural, so the verb has no -s.

exercises.prompt: The police ___ looking for the stolen car.
exercises.explanation: police is plural, so we say the police are.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: I need a new pair of jeans.
exercises.explanation: jeans is plural, so we say a pair of jeans or some new jeans.
